title: Implement one-writer control leases across the room and session services
description:
Purpose:
Enforce the one-writer rule without collapsing terminal input into the room sequencer.

Scope:
- Add room-side acquire/release control operations and durable lease records.
- Grant or reject leases through the room actor.
- Make the session transport accept input only when authenticated with the current `lease_epoch`.
- Broadcast lease changes so non-holders update UI and stop typing.

Deliverables:
- Lease grant/revoke flow across room and session services.
- Lease-epoch validation in the data plane.
- Client-facing lease state updates.

Required test plan coverage:
- Lease acquisition and release coverage.
- Competing writers conflict coverage.
- Revocation-after-lease-change coverage.
- Input rejection coverage for stale lease epochs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Only one client at a time can type into a session.
- Lease state is authoritative, recoverable, and enforced by the session service.
- The room still sequences only lease control, not terminal bytes.

Planning refinements (2026-03-15):
- Validate lease semantics as a cross-plane contract: cover acquire, release, revoke, epoch monotonicity, and stale-epoch rejection explicitly.
- Capture structured audit logs for conflicts, revocations, stale-input attempts, and holder changes.
- Add a repo-runnable verification script for competing writers and forced revocation scenarios.
notes:
Planning revision 2026-03-15:
- Validate lease semantics as a cross-plane contract. Unit tests should cover acquire/release/revoke and epoch monotonicity, while integration coverage should prove the session transport rejects stale epochs immediately.
- Capture structured audit logs for conflicts, revocations, stale-input attempts, and holder changes so lease bugs can be debugged from artifacts.
- Add a repo-runnable verification script under Scripts/ for competing writers and forced revocation scenarios.
close_reason: Enforced one-writer lease conflicts, lease fanout, and transport revocation

title: Implement a bootstrap-capable session backend and ordered output sequencing
description:
Purpose:
Satisfy the hard late-join requirement in the engineering plan by making the session backend capable of reconstructing current terminal state for a new subscriber.

Scope:
- Implement a bootstrap redraw path that emits a coherent redraw plus a live-stream anchor.
- Preserve per-session output ordering with explicit `output_seq` accounting.
- Use the local Ghostty tree and the zmx reference to shape a backend that can supervise long-lived terminal sessions without inventing a bespoke semantics-free process wrapper.

Deliverables:

- Output log/anchor contract.

Required test plan coverage:

- Ordered live-stream continuation after bootstrap.
- Bootstrap correctness across resize and long-running session cases.

Acceptance criteria:
- A fresh client can reconstruct terminal state from bootstrap bytes plus the live stream.
- Session output remains strictly ordered per session.
- The architecture no longer hand-waves late join as future work.

Planning refinements (2026-03-15):
- Build a bootstrap fixture corpus early: long-running output, resize history, wrapped lines, reconnect from a saved anchor, and other tricky redraw cases should be comparable from transcripts.
- Add deterministic coverage around output_seq and anchor handling plus a repo-runnable late-join script that logs bootstrap boundaries and live-stream continuation.

title: Implement draw-when-needed frame scheduling across camera, texture, and timer updates
description:

title: Persist control leases in durable room snapshots and recovery
description:
Problem
`RoomActor.recover` rebuilds `leaseBySessionID` only from journal records after `baseSnapshot.roomSeq`, but `DurableRoomSnapshot` currently persists only surfaces/render profiles. If an `acquire_control` is included in the latest snapshot window, recovery loses the active holder, lease epoch, and expiry until a later lease op appears in the journal tail. That breaks writer exclusivity after restart.

Observed code
- `host/DemoApp/RoomSchema.swift`: `DurableRoomSnapshot` has no lease payload.
- `host/DemoApp/RoomActor.swift`: `recover(...)` seeds actor state from the latest snapshot and only reapplies side effects from journal records after that snapshot sequence.

Required changes
- Extend the durable room snapshot schema to persist active control lease state needed for exact recovery, including holder identity and epoch semantics.
- Ensure snapshot write/recovery preserves active leases even when the relevant `acquire_control` happened before the latest snapshot.
- Preserve compatibility/validation rules for the updated schema and checksum path.

Unit tests
- Add a regression test in `host/Tests/DemoAppTests/RoomActorTests.swift` that acquires control, forces a snapshot, recovers with no lease ops in the journal tail, and asserts recovered lease state matches pre-restart state.
- Add schema/codec validation coverage in `host/Tests/DemoAppTests/RoomSchemaTests.swift` for the new snapshot lease fields.
- Add a test covering lease epoch behavior across snapshot/recovery boundaries so reacquire/release semantics remain monotonic.

E2E / integration verification
- Add a room persistence/recovery verification path that simulates restart from persisted snapshot + journal tail and proves exclusivity is preserved for an already-held session. This can be a Swift test or scripted harness invoked by the room verification lane, but it must exercise the persisted snapshot boundary rather than only in-memory replay.

Acceptance criteria
- Recovering from a snapshot taken after `acquire_control` restores the active holder and correct lease epoch without requiring later lease journal entries.
- Differential recovery behavior matches uninterrupted execution for lease state as well as surfaces.
close_reason: Durable room snapshots now persist active control leases and preserve lease epochs across recovery

title: Align Zig and Metal style with ghostty reference

title: Implement RoomActor journaling, snapshotting, and deterministic recovery
description:
Purpose:
Implement the single-writer room core that validates, sequences, persists, and recovers authoritative spatial state.

Scope:

Deliverables:

title: Implement per-session transport, auth tokens, and reconnect anchors
description:

title: Route keyboard, text, mouse, wheel, and paste input through Ghostty translation
description:

description:

title: Add metrics and structured logs for room, session, Ghostty, and compositor paths
description:

title: Define the durable room schema, op vocabulary, and persistence records

title: Integrate room/session orchestration into a coherent multi-client surface lifecycle
description:
Purpose:
Connect the room plane and session plane into one explicit user-facing surface lifecycle without re-defining lower-level transport, lease, or replay contracts inside UI glue.

Scope:
- Orchestrate create, attach, subscribe, disconnect, recover, and close flows across room, session, and client surfaces.
- Define and implement the surface lifecycle state machine: provisioning, attached, disconnected, degraded, error, and closing.
- Reconcile desired room state, actual session state, and client-visible state transitions without smearing cross-service policy into ad hoc callbacks.

Deliverables:
- Cross-service orchestration for create/attach/close/recover flows.

title: Spatial terminal canvas V1 execution plan from history/eng-plan.md
description:

title: Preserve pending redraws when MTKView temporarily lacks a drawable
description:
Problem
`CanvasView.Coordinator.draw(in:)` clears `FrameScheduler` state before confirming `view.currentDrawable` exists. During resize, occlusion, or app backgrounding, `MTKView` can temporarily return no drawable. In that case the invalidation is consumed and the canvas stays stale until some unrelated future event triggers another redraw.

Observed code
- `host/DemoApp/CanvasView.swift`: `guard frameScheduler.consumePendingDraw() != nil else { return }` runs before `guard let drawable = view.currentDrawable else { return }`.
- `host/DemoApp/FrameScheduler.swift`: `consumePendingDraw()` empties pending reasons and clears the scheduled flag immediately.

Required changes
- Make pending invalidations survive a no-drawable frame, either by only consuming after a drawable is acquired or by re-queueing the consumed reasons when `currentDrawable` is nil.
- Keep redraw scheduling behavior bounded so repeated nil-drawable frames do not spin unnecessarily.

Unit tests
- Add regression coverage around `FrameScheduler` and/or coordinator draw logic proving a pending invalidation remains pending after a failed draw attempt with no drawable.
- Add a follow-up assertion that once a drawable becomes available, the same invalidation is rendered exactly once.

E2E / integration verification
- Add an integration-style test or host-side harness that simulates consecutive draw callbacks with `currentDrawable == nil` followed by a valid drawable, and verifies the frame still renders after drawable recovery.
- Include this in the DemoApp verification lane if practical, or document the exact automated harness used.

Acceptance criteria
- Temporary drawable loss cannot permanently drop the latest invalidation.
- Once a drawable is available again, the pending frame is rendered without requiring a new external invalidation event.
close_reason: Pending redraws now survive nil-drawable draw attempts until a successful render completes
